items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Bobby Hackett asked me to come on the road with him to a place named Dunfy’s. ... I got in on the tail end of some really great careers. Venuti, Hackett, Zoot. ... I was out of Washington and off working with Hackett

ctx.x: Well let me just pick up here. So in the Washington club scene you were really getting exposed to a great variety of players. Is that a fair statement?

Well there were several really fine clubs. First of all Bohemian Caverns, and the late, great Tony Taylor who owned this place, he used to let me in there when I was underage and you could start drinking in Washington when you were 18 and he’d make sure that I didn’t get in too much trouble, you know. He kept me on a pretty short leash. He’d let me in because he knew I was just totally crazed about the music. And you know I was, many, many nights I was the only white kid, white person in the club maybe within…
